key_insight: ScienceIDE turns scientific code repositories into programmable environments that AI agents can learn from and act inside. This makes decades of scientific software and workflows more accessible for agent training, evaluation, and reliable automation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the 'scientific experience bottleneck': scientific code is rich in knowledge but hard for AI systems to learn from because toolchains are fragmented, domain conventions are implicit, and correctness requires specialized scientific criteria.
method: Builds infrastructure that converts scientific codebases into agent-learnable environments.
Uses expert-defined scientific guidance to encode workflows, constraints, and evaluation signals.
Provides a programmable interface so scientific agents can interact with code, tools, and tasks in a structured way.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ScienceIDE offers a path toward more realistic scientific agent training and benchmarking. It could improve automation in research workflows, code understanding, and domain-specific problem solving across scientific fields.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: scientific code repository -> ScienceIDE -> agent-learnable environment -> scientific agent
Before/after comparison showing fragmented code usage versus structured environment interaction
Icon set for code, tools, expert rules, agent, and evaluation metrics
Simple workflow schematic highlighting task execution, feedback, and correctness checking
paper_title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
paper_authors: Hejia Geng, Zesen Huang, Haoyang Li, Wenbin Li, Koutian Wu
